A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe the same PEARL and CALCONFLICTBENCH work. Main text, equations, seven figures, three tables, Algorithm 1, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original CALCONFLICTBENCH evaluations, PEARL training results, sensitivity analyses, and a model-response case study in Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–5 and 7.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark evaluations, PEARL results, sensitivity analyses, and case study, including the outcomes in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The Strategy Hub, rollout procedure in Algorithm 1, four reward components, curriculum, and round-wise GRPO training remain unchanged, including their appendix descriptions.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic academic/company calendar task, four-organization training/validation pool, and evaluation of ten users from two organizations. Appendix C.4's timestamp edits do not establish changed training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains identical model rows and ReAct/Mem+ReAct comparators. Table 2 retains the same zero-shot, SFT, and zero-shot plus StrategyHub comparisons with PEARL.

E3.justification: The metrics, M/W sweeps, evaluation sample counts, 80/20 split, and training/validation horizons remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendices D–E. The revised illustrative timestamps are not accompanied by a reported experimental protocol change.

E4.justification: The sensitivity and horizon analyses, Table 2 component comparisons, and doctor-appointment case study in Appendix D.3/Figure 7 are unchanged. Appendix C.4 edits example input metadata without adding or revising an analysis.

E5.justification: Table 1 still reports averaging over ten independent instances. Neither version changes run or seed information, uncertainty reporting, or statistical testing practices.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings match throughout both versions. For example, Table 2 retains PEARL's AER of 0.12 and ERR of 0.761, versus SFT's 0.27 and 0.325; the appendix case-study outcomes also match.

T1.justification: The formal task, ORD definition, reward curriculum, return and advantage equations, and Appendix C data-generation formalization are unchanged. No proofs or theoretical results are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same task, benchmark, and PEARL contributions, including the claimed 0.76 error reduction rate and 55% improvement over the strongest baseline.

C2.justification: Interpretations of preference adaptation, memory access, and training remain unchanged, as do the case-study explanations. The limitations concerning synthetic preferences, unobserved real-world influences, experimental coverage, and context length are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C.4 changes the example reading group's end time from 14:44 to 15:44 and the workshop's from 14:33 to 15:33. These revise documented example metadata; prompts, tool schemas, hyperparameters, hardware, and the project address otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and Section 6 positioning relative to scheduling assistants, planning agents, preference alignment, and external memory are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 changes Niran Kundapur's affiliation from Eightfold.ai to Viven, removes the front-page date, relocates contact information, and moves the acknowledgment before References. The scientific prose and section sequence otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the decorated title and full-width boxed abstract with a compact header and column-width abstract. Figures and appendix boxes shift with text reflow, including Figure 1 moving from page 3 to page 2; figure content, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix C.4's extended workshop end time makes it overlap every other candidate event; in v3 it ended before two candidates began. This improves the example's consistency with the stated mutually conflicting-event setup. The gain is limited: scientific methods, results, and limitations remain unchanged, while the other edits mainly affect presentation.
